content: Before I print anything, take another look at your design. Send me the design again with submit_design, changed or unchanged. I'll print the final part from what you send.

reasoning:
I'm checking the design for problems, starting with the bolt head sitting in its pocket on the underside. The pocket depth looks fine, but the head is 15 wide in a 17-wide pocket and only 5.5 deep, so it sits nearly flush and would be hard to grip with a finger.

I'm working through the remaining checks: the slot's signature and orientation look right, the XZ profile extrudes to the full plate length, and the 27 mm slot fits inside the 50 mm plate. Last, I'm weighing whether the 3.5 mm floor leaves enough thread engagement, since the bolt length is still unknown.

I'm weighing the thread engagement again, since the bolt length still decides whether there's enough. I'm also considering a stepped coupon with several widths so one print can find the fit, though the unknown jaw gap makes that a guess.

I'm considering a stepped coupon with widths at w-4, w-2, w, and so on, so one print can find the right fit. The pieces would be separate bodies laid out in a row, though I'm wary of the complexity.

I'm wrapping up the coupon idea: a row of five steps from w-4 to w+4, each 12 mm long and 3 mm apart, unioned into one workplane, with the smallest step first in the manual. I'm leaving the head clearance at 2 and the plate thickness as it is, and I'll add a coupon_step parameter and update the manual before resubmitting.

Still writing the coupon code...

I'm resubmitting the fit coupon as a row of five slices spanning 4 mm either side of my guessed width, so one print shows which width suits your clamp.

    w=p.plate_w; t=p.plate_t; b=p.bevel
    pts=[(-w/2+b,0),(w/2-b,0),(w/2,b),(w/2,t),(-w/2,t),(-w/2,b)]
    body=cq.Workplane('XZ').polyline(pts).close().extrude(p.plate_len/2, both=True)
    depth=p.head_h+p.head_extra
    pocket=(cq.Workplane('XY').slot2D(p.slot_travel+p.head_d+p.head_clear, p.head_d+p.head_clear, 90).extrude(depth))
    thru=(cq.Workplane('XY').slot2D(p.slot_travel+p.bolt_d+p.shank_clear, p.bolt_d+p.shank_clear, 90).extrude(t))
    return body.cut(pocket).cut(thru)
"},{"id":"plate-coupon","role":"coupon","material":"PLA (black)","print_orientation":"Bevelled narrow face on the bed","use_orientation":"Try each slice in the tripod clamp, narrowest first, to find the width that drops in and is gripped firmly","code":"def build(p):
    t=p.plate_t; b=p.bevel; L=p.coupon_len; gap=3
    res=None
    for i in range(5):
        w=p.plate_w+(i-2)*p.coupon_step
        pts=[(-w/2+b,0),(w/2-b,0),(w/2,b),(w/2,t),(-w/2,t),(-w/2,b)]
        piece=cq.Workplane('XZ').polyline(pts).close().extrude(L/2, both=True).translate((0,(i-2)*(L+gap),0))
        res=piece if res is None else res.union(piece)
    return res

Slide the plate along the slot to balance the camera, then tighten.","parts":["plate"],"hardware":["webcam-bolt"]},{"n":"5","text":"Drop the plate into the tripod clamp from above and tighten the clamp knob. Don't over-tighten. Check it's secure before letting go of the camera.","parts":["plate"]}], "questions": [{"text":"What is the jaw-to-jaw gap and the angle of the clamp lips? I couldn't get numbers, so plate_w=38 mm and a 45 degree 3 mm bevel are guesses."},{"text":"What is the length of the jaw slot, and does the clamp have a locating pin or stop?"},{"text":"How long is the threaded part of the webcam bolt? It needs to reach about 6 mm into the camera after passing through the plate's 3.5 mm floor."},{"text":"Can you get your fingers or a tool on the bolt head? If it has no knob or hex, the pocket may need a driver slot."}], "note": "Printing a 1/4-20 screw in PLA would be weak, so the "part that screws in" is the webcam bolt you already have. The plate is a flat dovetail-style plate with a slot and a pocket for the bolt head. It is a temporary substitute for a camera plate. I couldn't get any dimensions of the tripod clamp, so plate width, length and bevel are guesses. Print the five-width fit coupon first. Until you've tested it with a light load, don't trust an expensive camera to it. A real plate may have a pin or stop that this one lacks."}
